sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5159 Of 2019
Order:

1. The petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.232 of 2019 of Tenali Rural Police Station, Guntur district, which was registered for the offences under Sections 188, 420, 270, 272, 273 and 328 of IPC and Sections 56, 57(i) and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').

entities.text: Tenali Rural Police Station, Guntur district
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that, on 23.08.2019 at 14.00 hours, on receiving the credible information, the complainant suo motu registered the case against the petitioners/Accused Nos.1 and 2 on the ground that A-1 is in possession of the banned tobacco products, having purchased the same from A-2, selling them to public on higher price with their deceitful words and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R., and remanded them to judicial custody for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He UDPR,J relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police, Tenali Rural Police Station.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the Petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offences under Chittithula Gopaiah vs The State Of Ap on 16 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186856967/
